blockingFindings.title: The declared python3 -B trust boundary permits process-start environment initialization before any pin verification
blockingFindings.finding: Both binding conformance commands and checker usage prescribe python3 -B. Under that exact invocation, Python honors PYTHONPATH and imports sitecustomize during interpreter startup. A controlled local marker was observed before the checker, after which the exact checker still verified 19 pins and returned contract OK. The isolated -I -B control left the same marker absent and passed.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: Arbitrary pre-auth code can monkeypatch hashing, file reads, import machinery or reviewed inputs before DeferredAuthorityLoader exists. Consequently, success under the declared command does not prove that the reported hash-before-execution sequence occurred in a trustworthy interpreter. This is the same boundary the candidate describes as hostile-environment evidence, and no binding external isolated-launch precondition narrows it.
blockingFindings.whyAuthoredCheckerMissedIt: Its environment probes synthesize hostile sys.modules, path-swap and pyc state only after the current interpreter and all explicit stdlib imports already started. They prove the verified retained-source loader, not process startup. The disposable RT14 child is also launched with -B but without -I.
blockingFindings.positiveBoundary: Once interpreter startup and early imports are trusted, all independently exercised pin, review, buffer, pyc, sys.modules and path-swap properties passed. This finding does not reopen the canonical raw repair, RT14 API repair, D9 taxonomy, goldens or reducer semantics.
blockingFindings.impact: v1.12 cannot be the accepted checker authority for RT15/E8 or architecture freeze. Treating it as accepted would allow an untrusted launch environment to run before, and potentially falsify, the very checker meant to authenticate the retained D9 chain.
blockingFindings.requiredRepair: Create v1.13 without editing v1.12. Pin this exact REJECT review; make caller-owned python3 -I -B the sole declared conformance invocation; put import sys plus an early sys.flags.isolated refusal before other explicit imports as a defensive unsupported-mode refusal; and require isolated argv at every new nested/disposable subprocess boundary. Add process-start sitecustomize/PYTHONPATH controls proving nonisolated mode is unsupported and isolated mode prevents the marker. Do not claim the in-script flag check prevents code that already ran before script entry—the security guarantee comes from the caller's -I launch.

Use isolated argv for every subprocess launch reachable from v1.13 conformance, including disposable RT14 probes and any retained-suite wrapper. Do not leave a nested sys.executable -B escape.

retainedPositiveConclusions: D9V111-PF-01 is correctly repaired in v1.12: all 17 inherited lexical tokens and every protected raw span match v1.10.
The exact ordered v1.12 object projects to v1.11 and then semantically to v1.10 with no unauthorized D9 change.
The complete frozen RT14 access surface is present, authenticated, arity-correct and behaviorally compatible.
All 45 goldens, four contextual rows, class/code/exit maps and 399600 reducer cases retain their declared semantics.
The retained-source loader is fail-closed against pin/review corruption, disk swaps, pyc and preloaded module substitution after trustworthy interpreter startup.
The validator is total over the 2265 systematic JSON-shape probes and public check is controlled over malformed authority/candidate arguments.

residuals.text: Even an isolated Python checker is an architecture test instrument, not the Rust production enforcement mechanism. Downstream callers must pin the accepted checker bytes and own the isolated launcher.
The binding's stated blind-second-author, precedence-judgment, identifier-placeholder, combination-coverage and implementation-demonstration limitations remain unchanged.

limitations: The review did not claim an untrusted operating system, Python executable, system stdlib, or same-process debugger boundary. The blocking falsifier is the narrower launch environment the candidate itself admits by prescribing python3 -B.
The 399600 reducer domain is substantial and closed-vocabulary-derived, not a mathematical enumeration of arbitrary Python objects.
The disposable RT14 rebind changes only checker identity pins and proves API compatibility; it is not a full RT15 candidate.
Green checker and review results do not demonstrate the Rust implementation or release qualification.

forbiddenConsequences: no RT15 authoring against v1.12 as accepted authority
